summary: Gustaf John Ramstedt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1898) under Otto Donner, J. N. Reuter, and Eemil Nestor Setälä, later serving there as professor (1917–1941) and at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

Gustav Bickell was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and earned his Ph.D. at Marburg (1857–1862). He held posts at Marburg, Giessen, Münster, Innsbruck (1874), and the University of Vienna (1891).

Gustav Ecke specialized in sinology and history/archaeology, earning a Ph.D. at Erlangen-Nuremberg after studying at Bonn, Berlin, and under Joseph Hackin. He taught at Xiamen, Tsinghua, Fu Jen, and served as curator in Honolulu before becoming an arts professor at Hawaiʻi (1950–1966).

Gustav Friedrich Oehler was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tübingen and Berlin under Ludwig Heinrich Kapff and Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Basel Mission Seminary, Tübingen (1838), Schöntal Seminary, and Breslau.

Gustav Haloun worked in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Prague, he held posts at Charles University, Halle-Wittenberg, and Göttingen, before serving as Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Herbig was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Munich, completing his Ph.D. and habilitation at Munich. He worked as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library (1899–1913) and was an ordinary professor at Rostock, Breslau, and Munich.

Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto and Friedrich Heiler, later holding professorships at the University of Latvia (1927–1935), Kiel (1935–1936), and the University of Bonn.

Gustav Meyer was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Breslau (~1867–1871) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. After posts at Ernestinum Gotha, Kleinseitner Gymnasium, and Charles University, he served as associate professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Graz (1877–1897).

Gustav Roth was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Munich and studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle, and Patna. He was an Akademischer Oberrat at Göttingen (1965–1981) and Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bonn, Leipzig, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D.). He served at the Bodleian and Royal Libraries, as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency University (1872–1894), and at the University of Berlin.

Gustave Liétard worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Collège de Toul, earned a Dr.med. at the University of Strasbourg (~1851–1858), and studied under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. His career includes an affiliation with Villanova University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Gustavo Moura specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned a bachelor's at the University of Chester, a master's at Federal University of Paraíba, and a Ph.D. in Religious Studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (2018–2022).

Gustaw Blatt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University (Ph.D.) under Lucjan Malinowski and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, Ernst Windisch, and August Leskien. He served at the Jewish Gymnasium in Brody and as professor at Lviv (from 1910).

Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky. His academic posts include positions at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and the Leiden University Centre for Linguistics (2016).

Guy Bugault worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, having studied under Olivier Lacombe. He held a post at Paris Nanterre University (~1965–1969) and was Professor of Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1969–1985).

Guy G. Stroumsa is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Paris, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, EPHE, and Harvard (Ph.D. 1978). He held faculty posts at Hebrew University and was Professor of the Study of the Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studying also under several Tibetan teachers, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Guybon Henry Damant was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.A. at Christ's College, Cambridge (1864–1868), where he studied under John Peile and Edward Byles Cowell.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
